{{Short description|Italian mathematician and writer}}
{{Orphan|date=January 2021}}
'''Ottavio Scarlattini''' (1623 – 1699) was an Italian [[Philosophy|philosopher]], [[mathematician]] and [[theologian]].<ref name="Fantuzzi">{{Cite encyclopedia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cQThWI4kr4wC&pg=PA355|title= Scarlattini Ottavio|pages=355–359|language=Italian|encyclopedia=Notizie degli Scrittori Bolognesi|publisher= Stamperia di S. Tommaso D'Aquino|year=1789|location=Bologna|volume=7|first=Giovanni|last=Fantuzzi}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Ottavio Scarlattini became a [[Canon Regular of the Lateran]] at [[Bologna]] in 1639, and then he was appointed [[Archpriest]] of Villa Fontana in [[Medicina]].<ref name="Fantuzzi" /> Scarlattini's 1679 publication ''Dell'Epicuro contro gli epicurei'' was an 830 page treatise arguing for the [[beatification]] of [[Epicurus]] in which he defended [[Epicureanism]] as a philosophy.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=q3wfEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Ottavio+Scarlattini%22&pg=PA1238|title=History of Italian Philosophy|page=1238|isbn=9789401205221|publisher=[[Brill Publishers]]|author=[[Eugenio Garin]]|year=2008}}</ref> Translated into Latin, the work became well known across Europe.<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A3xGEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Ottavio+Scarlattini%22&pg=PA373|title=Templa serena: studi in onore di Enrico Flores|chapter=Una conversione epicurea nel sec. XVII: Ottavio Scarlattini, i due Epicuri e Lucrezio dimenticato|author=Guido Milanese|editor=Mariantonietta Paladini|isbn=9788868871017|year=2021|publisher=[[University of Naples Federico II|Federico II University Press]]|page=373}}</ref> His 1683 publication ''L'huomo, e sue parti figurato, e simbolico, anatomico, rationale, morale, mistico, politico, e legale'' was a discourse on the symbolism of the parts of the human body; giving each part an anatomical, rational, moral, mystic, political, and legal analysis.<ref>{{cite book|title=Mediaeval Backgrounds of the Elizabethan Emblem-book|author=David Mason Greene|year=1958|page=48|publisher=University of California, Berkeley}}</ref>
